questions.question: In MS Word, which command allows users to duplicate a selected block of text and place the copy at a different location within the same document or another document?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copy and Paste**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Copy and Paste** is a widely used command in MS Word and other text editing software to duplicate text and place it in another location within the document or across documents.
 
• Users can select the text, right-click to copy, and then paste it at the desired location using the right-click menu or shortcut keys (Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V).
 
• This command allows users to retain the original text while creating a duplicate copy, ensuring no data is lost.
 
• Copy and Paste is applicable to not just text but also images, tables, and other elements in MS Word.
 
• It simplifies repetitive tasks and enhances productivity by eliminating the need for retyping or recreating content.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cut vs. Copy:**

 
 
• The Cut command (Ctrl+X) removes the selected text or object from its original location and allows it to be pasted elsewhere.
 
• Copy (Ctrl+C), on the other hand, creates a duplicate while leaving the original content intact.
 
 
 
• **Drag and Drop Functionality:**
 
 
• Users can drag selected text or objects and drop them into a new location within the same document.
 
• This method is quick but lacks the precision of Copy and Paste for cross-document transfers.
 
 
 
• **Paste Special:**
 
 
• Paste Special allows users to control the formatting of copied content when pasting.
 
• For example, users can paste as plain text, formatted text, or in other specified formats.
 
 
 
• **Shortcut Keys in MS Word:**
 
 
• Common shortcuts include Ctrl+C (Copy), Ctrl+V (Paste), Ctrl+X (Cut), and Ctrl+Z (Undo).
 
• These shortcuts are designed to enhance user efficiency and streamline text manipulation tasks.
 
 
 
• **Clipboard Functionality:**
 
 
• The Clipboard temporarily stores copied or cut items, allowing users to paste them multiple times.
 
• In MS Word, the Clipboard can hold multiple items, offering extended flexibility for editing tasks.

questions.question: How many total islands/islets/rocky outcrops are there in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands as per the Andaman and Nicobar Administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**836**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are a group of islands located in the Bay of Bengal, consisting of a total of **836 islands/islets/rocky outcrops** as per the Andaman and Nicobar Administration.
 
• The archipelago is divided into two groups: the Andaman Islands (north) and the Nicobar Islands (south).
 
• These islands are known for their rich biodiversity, unique flora and fauna, and strategic importance for India's maritime boundaries.
 
• Of the 836 islands, only a fraction are inhabited, while the majority remain pristine and untouched.
 
• These islands form a vital ecological hotspot and are protected under various environmental laws and conservation programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Significance**

 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie at the juncture of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea, making them strategically important for India's defense and trade.
 
• They act as a natural barrier to the Indian coastline, protecting it from potential threats and offering a vantage point for maritime surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity**
 
 
• The islands are part of the Indo-Malayan eco-zone, hosting a variety of endemic species, including rare birds, reptiles, and marine life.
 
• The tropical rainforests here support diverse ecosystems, with mangroves playing a key role in stabilizing coastal environments.
 
 
 
• **Tribes of the Islands**
 
 
• The islands are home to indigenous tribes such as the Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarwa, and Sentinelese.
 
• These tribes have distinct cultural practices and lifestyles, and efforts are made to preserve their heritage and isolation.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Conservation**
 
 
• The islands are a popular tourist destination, known for their beaches, coral reefs, and adventure activities like scuba diving.
 
• Significant areas are designated as protected zones, such as the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, to conserve the delicate ecosystems.

questions.question: Which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act has NOT amended anything in the Directive Principles of the State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**48th Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **48th Amendment Act** of 1984 did not amend any provisions related to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• This amendment was enacted to extend the President's Rule in the state of Punjab beyond the one-year limit prescribed under Article 356(5) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It dealt specifically with the political situation in Punjab and had no relevance to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• In contrast, amendments like the **42nd Amendment Act** and **86th Amendment Act** directly addressed and modified provisions of the DPSP.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, for instance, added new principles, while the **86th Amendment Act** integrated the right to education for children under Article 21A, influencing related DPSPs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• Enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution, DPSPs aim to establish a welfare state by guiding the government in policy-making.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced in a court of law, but they are fundamental in governance.
 
• Examples include provisions for social welfare, equitable distribution of resources, and environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution," it made significant changes to the DPSP.
 
• Added Articles 39A (Equal justice and free legal aid), 43A (Workers' participation in management), and 48A (Protection of the environment).
 
• Shifted the focus towards socialism and environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act (2002):**
 
 
• Introduced Article 21A, making the right to education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Modified Article 45 under DPSP to focus on early childhood care for children below six years.
 
 
 
• **97th Amendment Act (2011):**
 
 
• Added a new DPSP under Article 43B, emphasizing the promotion of cooperative societies.
 
• Aimed to strengthen cooperative movements in India by ensuring their democratic functioning.

questions.question: In India, which region is NOT suitable for tube-well irrigation due to non-alluvial tracts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plateau regions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plateau regions** in India, such as the **Deccan Plateau**, are characterized by hard rock formations and non-alluvial soil, making them unsuitable for tube-well irrigation.
 
• Tube-well irrigation requires **soft, porous, and permeable alluvial soil** to facilitate water extraction, which is not present in plateau regions.
 
• These regions often lack sufficient groundwater recharge due to rocky terrain and limited aquifer systems.
 
• In contrast, regions like Punjab, Western Uttar Pradesh, and Coastal Plains have fertile alluvial soil and abundant groundwater, making them ideal for tube-well irrigation.
 
• Farmers in plateau regions primarily depend on rainfall or surface water sources such as tanks, reservoirs, and rivers for irrigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil and Irrigation:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is formed by river deposits and is rich in nutrients, making it fertile and ideal for agriculture.
 
• Its porous structure allows easy water percolation, which facilitates the use of tube-well irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater and Aquifers:**
 
 
• Groundwater is stored in aquifers, which are layers of permeable rock or sediment that can hold and transmit water.
 
• Plateau regions typically have fractured or impermeable rocks that hinder groundwater storage and extraction.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau Characteristics:**
 
 
• It is composed of igneous and metamorphic rocks, which are hard and non-porous.
 
• These features limit the region’s ability to support groundwater-based irrigation systems like tube-wells.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Irrigation in Plateau Regions:**
 
 
• Farmers rely on surface irrigation methods such as canals, tanks, and rainwater harvesting to meet their agricultural water needs.
 
• Government initiatives promote micro-irrigation techniques like drip and sprinkler systems to optimize water use in these areas.
 
 
 
• **Indian Irrigation Practices:**
 
 
• Approximately 48% of India’s net sown area relies on irrigation, with tube-wells being a major source in alluvial regions.
 
• Regions unsuitable for tube-well irrigation often implement watershed development projects to improve water availability.

questions.question: A water tank can be filled in 29 minutes by using 23 pipes of the same capacity. In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 47 pipes of the same capacity as above?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Apply the **Inverse Proportion** rule: **M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂**

Here, **23 pipes × 29 minutes = 47 pipes × Time**

Time = (23 × 29) ÷ 47 = 667 ÷ 47

Time ≈ 14.19 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 14.19 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (**M₁**) = 23

Initial time (**T₁**) = 29 minutes

Final number of pipes (**M₂**) = 47

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Pipes × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of tank = 23 × 29 units

⇒ Total capacity = 667 units

⇒ Time taken by 47 pipes = Total capacity ÷ Number of pipes

⇒ Time = 667 ÷ 47

⇒ Time = 14.19148...

⇒ Time ≈ 14.19 minutes (rounded off to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 14.19 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation

In **Pipes and Cisterns**, the number of pipes is inversely proportional to the time taken to fill the tank (if all pipes have the same efficiency).

Chain Rule Formula

The general formula is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is efficiency/pipes, D is days/minutes, and W is work/capacity.</p

questions.question: Which country lies to the east of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:

• The border between Arunachal Pradesh and Myanmar is demarcated by the **India-Myanmar International Boundary**.
 
• The border region is characterized by dense forests and mountainous terrain, making it strategically and geographically significant.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh also shares international borders with **China** to the north and Bhutan to the west, but Myanmar lies directly to its east.
 
• This area includes tribal communities and is part of the larger Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bordering States and Countries:**

 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh shares its borders with three countries: **China, Bhutan, and Myanmar**.
 
• It also shares state borders with Assam and Nagaland within India.
 
 
 
• **McMahon Line:**
 
 
• The McMahon Line is the de facto boundary between India and China in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• This line is a source of territorial disputes between India and China.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Diversity:**
 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is home to numerous indigenous tribes, including the Adi, Nyishi, Apatani, and Mishmi tribes.
 
• These tribes have unique cultures, traditions, and languages.

questions.question: Which organisation does the Ministry of Rural Development cooperate with for rural development in Asia and the Pacific?

options.text: Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and Pacific (CIRDAP)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and Pacific (CIRDAP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ministry of Rural Development in India collaborates with the **Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and the Pacific (CIRDAP)** to advance rural development initiatives in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• CIRDAP was established in **1979** at the initiative of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations to promote integrated rural development.
 
• The organization has its headquarters in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**, and works with member countries to strengthen rural development policies and practices.
 
• India is a founding member of CIRDAP and actively contributes to its programs focusing on poverty alleviation, sustainable agriculture, and rural infrastructure development.
 
• CIRDAP functions as a platform for knowledge-sharing, capacity-building, and technical cooperation among its **15 member countries**, including India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CIRDAP Member Countries**

 
 
• CIRDAP has **15 member countries**, which include Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Iran, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and Vietnam.
 
• These countries collaborate on rural development strategies and share best practices to improve living conditions in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Rural Development**
 
 
• Integrated rural development involves a holistic approach to improving economic, social, and environmental conditions in rural areas.
 
• It focuses on sectors such as agriculture, education, health, infrastructure, and community participation to ensure sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Role of FAO**
 
 
• The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations was instrumental in the establishment of CIRDAP, emphasizing its commitment to eradicating hunger and promoting rural development globally.
 
• FAO continues to provide technical support and guidance to CIRDAP and its member countries.
 
 
 
• **India and CIRDAP**
 
 
• India’s Ministry of Rural Development plays a pivotal role in supporting CIRDAP by offering expertise, resources, and research inputs.
 
• India often hosts training programs, workshops, and conferences under the aegis of CIRDAP to foster regional cooperation in rural development.

questions.question: Babita travels a certain distance at a speed of 11 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 44 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 34 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial distance is 44 km (LCM of 11 and 44).

**Total Distance** = 44 (forward 1) + 88 (forward 2) + 132 (return) = 264 km.

**Total Time** = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 264 ÷ 34 = 132/17 hours.

**Forward Time** = (44/11) + (88/44) = 4 + 2 = 6 hours.

**Return Speed** = 132 ÷ (132/17 − 6) = 132 ÷ (30/17) = 132 × 17 ÷ 30 = 74.8 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.8 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bc5c2f7239546ef5fbaf650ec5951497997ce496ebf4c0f5da45e9387b67205.png] 

**Given:** Forward speed 1 = 11 km/hr, Forward speed 2 = 44 km/hr, Avg Speed = 34 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let first distance be D. Second distance = 2D. Total return distance = 3D.

⇒ Total Distance = D + 2D + 3D = 6D.

⇒ Total Time = (D/11) + (2D/44) + (3D/V) = (4D+2D)/44 + 3D/V = 6D/44 + 3D/V = 3D/22 + 3D/V.

⇒ 34 = 6D ÷ (3D/22 + 3D/V) = 6D ÷ [3D(1/22 + 1/V)]

⇒ 34 = 2 ÷ ( (V + 22) / 22V )

⇒ 34 = 44V ÷ (V + 22)

⇒ 34(V + 22) = 44V ⇒ 34V + 748 = 44V

⇒ 10V = 748 ⇒ V = 74.8 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.8 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

For different distances d₁, d₂, d₃... with speeds s₁, s₂, s₃..., Average Speed = (Σd) ÷ (Σd/s).

Special Case: Equal Distances

When two equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, the average speed is (2ab) ÷ (a + b).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A person saves 40% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹960, then his income (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Savings** = 40% ⇒ **Expenditure** = 100% − 40% = 60%

60% units = ₹960

1% unit = 960 ÷ 60 = 16

100% units (**Income**) = 16 × 100 = ₹1600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Savings percentage** = 40%

**Expenditure** = ₹960

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e10e66e10bbdfe47d01ff9a2dfe55a1bd5620295422f2ccddc56701bc0b70370.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **total income** be ₹x.

⇒ **Savings** = 40% of x

⇒ **Expenditure** = **Income** − **Savings**

⇒ **Expenditure** = 100% − 40% = 60% of x

⇒ 60/100 × x = 960

⇒ 0.6x = 960

⇒ x = 960 ÷ 0.6

⇒ x = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

To calculate percentage change, use the formula: (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Income Components

In most aptitude problems, Income is always considered as the sum of Expenditure and Savings (I = E + S).

Base Value

Income is generally treated as the base (100%) when calculating percentage savings or percentage expenditure.

questions.question: If goods are purchased at ₹450 and (1)/(3) are sold at a loss of 10%, at what gain percentage should the remainder be sold so as to gain 20% on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the total quantity is 3 units. 1 unit is sold at 10% loss (−10%).

To get a 20% gain on the whole transaction (3 units), total profit needed = 3 × 20% = 60%.

Remaining units = 3 − 1 = 2 units.

Profit needed from remaining units = Total Profit − Profit/Loss already made = 60% − (−10%) = 70%.

Gain percentage on remainder = 70% ÷ 2 = 35%.

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total CP = ₹450 | Loss on 1/3rd part = 10% | Overall Gain = 20%.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | SP = CP × (100 − L%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1d0c335b5d91af0553f8cc97bd2912c5451131240beadb9403f65339243750b.png] 
⇒ Total SP required = 450 × (120 ÷ 100) = ₹540.
⇒ CP of 1/3rd goods = 450 × (1 ÷ 3) = ₹150.
⇒ SP of 1/3rd goods at 10% loss = 150 × (90 ÷ 100) = ₹135.
⇒ Remaining SP needed = 540 − 135 = ₹405.
⇒ CP of remaining 2/3rd goods = 450 − 150 = ₹300.
⇒ Profit required on remaining = 405 − 300 = ₹105.
⇒ Profit % on remaining = (105 ÷ 300) × 100 = 35%.
**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

For parts of goods, Overall % = (n₁ × p₁ + n₂ × p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where p is profit/loss %.

When the total CP is given but the question asks for a percentage, the actual CP value does not affect the final percentage result.

questions.question: In one of his famous works, Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of _____ was a descendant of the Prophet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sayyid Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Sayyid Dynasty** ruled the Delhi Sultanate from **1414 to 1451 CE **and was established after the decline of the Tughlaq Dynasty.
 
• **Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi**, in his famous work ***Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi***, claimed that the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty, **Khizr Khan**, was a **descendant of the Prophet Muhammad**.
 
• Khizr Khan was appointed as the **governor of Multan by Timur** (Tamerlane) and later established his rule in Delhi in 1414 CE.
 
• The dynasty is called "Sayyid" due to the belief that its rulers were **Sayyids**, descendants of the Prophet Muhammad, which is a title signifying high religious and social status in Islamic tradition.
 
• After Khizr Khan, his successors, including Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah, and Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah, ruled until the dynasty was overthrown by the Lodi Dynasty in 1451 CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi Sultanate**

 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate refers to a series of Muslim dynasties that ruled over large parts of India from **1206 to 1526 CE**.
 
• The Sultanate saw five main dynasties: **Slave (Mamluk), Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi** dynasties.
 
• The Sayyid Dynasty was the fourth dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Khizr Khan**
 
 
• Khizr Khan was the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty and ruled from 1414 to 1421 CE.
 
• He did not assume the title of Sultan and continued to acknowledge the suzerainty of Timur's successors in Central Asia.
 
• He focused on consolidating power in Delhi and surrounding areas rather than expanding the empire.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Sayyid Title**
 
 
• The title "Sayyid" denotes a person who claims direct lineage to the Prophet Muhammad through his grandsons Hasan and Husayn.
 
• This lineage is considered sacred in Islamic culture and conveys religious and social prestige.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Sayyid Dynasty**
 
 
• The Sayyid Dynasty faced continuous challenges, including revolts and weakened central authority.
 
• The last ruler, Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah, voluntarily abdicated the throne in favor of Bahlul Lodi in 1451 CE, marking the end of the dynasty.

questions.question: Find roots of 5m² + 18m + 16 = 0
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the **roots** of 5m² + 18m + 16 = 0, identify two numbers with **product** (5 × 16) = 80 and **sum** = 18.

The numbers are 10 and 8.

**Shortcut:** Divide these numbers by the **coefficient** of m² (5) and reverse their signs.

Roots = −(10/5) and −(8/5) ⇒ −2 and −8/5.

**∴ The correct answer is −8/5 and −2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The **quadratic equation** is 5m² + 18m + 16 = 0.

**Formula:** We use the **factorisation method** by splitting the middle term.

⇒ 5m² + 10m + 8m + 16 = 0

⇒ 5m(m + 2) + 8(m + 2) = 0

⇒ (5m + 8)(m + 2) = 0

Setting each **factor** to zero:

⇒ 5m + 8 = 0 ⇒ m = −8/5

⇒ m + 2 = 0 ⇒ m = −2

The **roots** of the equation are −8/5 and −2.

**∴ The correct answer is −8/5 and −2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the **discriminant** D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots. If D > 0, roots are **real and distinct**; if D = 0, roots are **real and equal**.

Sum and Product of Roots

The **Sum of roots** (α + β) = −b/a and the **Product of roots** (αβ) = c/a.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can also be found using x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.</p

questions.question: Rishi has ₹1,612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Shan and Piyush and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. It was seen that Shan and Piyush got the same amount after 19 and 20 years, respectively. How much (in ₹) did Rishi give to Shan?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Shan's share (S)** to **Piyush's share (P)** is given by (1 + R/100)Δt : 1.

Here, difference in time (Δt) = 20 − 19 = 1 year and Rate (R) = 8%.

Ratio S : P = (1 + 8/100)¹ : 1 ⇒ 108 : 100 ⇒ 27 : 25.

Total units = 27 + 25 = 52 units → ₹1,612.

1 unit = 1612 ÷ 52 = ₹31.

**Shan's share** = 27 × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = **₹1,612** | Rate (R) = **8% p.a.**

Time for **Shan** (n₁) = **19 years** | Time for **Piyush** (n₂) = **20 years**.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e90e2f39558c447e384a5e5838c968db76963e3df06033c22ee2b701d6b48c20.png] 

Let the amount given to **Shan** be S and to **Piyush** be P.

⇒ S(1 + 8/100)¹⁹ = P(1 + 8/100)²⁰

⇒ S = P(1 + 8/100)²⁰−¹⁹

⇒ S = P(108/100)

⇒ S/P = 27/25

⇒ S = [27 / (27 + 25)] × 1612

⇒ S = (27 / 52) × 1612

⇒ S = 27 × 31

⇒ S = **₹837**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Ratio Rule

When a sum is divided such that amounts are equal after T₁ and T₂ years, the ratio of shares is (1 + R/100)T²−T¹ : 1.

Effective Rate for CI

For a rate R% for 2 years, the effective rate is R + R + (R×R)/100 %.

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is essentially a **successive percentage increase** on the principal amount every year.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked his goods at X% above their cost price and sold them at a discount of 10%. If he gained 71% profit, then find the value of X.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the relationship: **(100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%) = MP ÷ CP**.

Given **Profit = 71%** and **Discount = 10%**.

MP ÷ CP = (100 + 71) ÷ (100 − 10) = 171 ÷ 90 = 19 ÷ 10.

Marked up value = 19 − 10 = 9 units on a base of 10.

Markup percentage X = (9 ÷ 10) × 100 = 90%.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Discount = 10%**, **Profit = 71%**, **Markup = X%**.
Formulas: **SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100** | **SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a1d5a570368c560993557f3bae67fe8b802fd1cc80e11faf455e08737f80297.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.
⇒ Since gain is 71%, **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 71 = 171.
⇒ Discount is 10%, so **SP = 90% of Marked Price (MP)**.
⇒ 171 = 0.90 × MP ⇒ MP = 171 ÷ 0.9 = 190.
⇒ **Markup (X)** = MP − CP = 190 − 100 = 90.
⇒ Since CP was 100, the markup percentage **X = 90%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relation

The effective percentage change can be calculated using the formula: **Net % = a + b + (ab ÷ 100)**, where 'a' is markup % and 'b' is discount % (negative).

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on **MP**, while **Profit/Loss** is calculated on **CP**.</p

questions.question: X is directly proportional to A² and A is inversely proportional to Y. If X is 97 when Y is 6, find X when Y is 2.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: **X ∝ A²** and **A ∝ 1/Y**.

Combining these, **X ∝ (1/Y)²** ⇒ **X ∝ 1/Y²**.

Relationship: **X₁ × Y₁² = X₂ × Y₂²**.

97 × 6² = X₂ × 2² ⇒ 97 × 36 = X₂ × 4.

X₂ = 97 × 9 = 873.

**∴ The correct answer is 873.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe43db152a68c34a3000a70f93f9aff48ccad32c4bb4ba35850d6243098157a0.png] 

**Given:** X₁ = 97, Y₁ = 6, Y₂ = 2.

**Formula Used:** X = k/Y² or X₁Y₁² = X₂Y₂²

⇒ X ∝ A² and A ∝ 1/Y ⇒ A² ∝ 1/Y²

⇒ Therefore, X ∝ 1/Y²

⇒ 97 = k / 6²

⇒ k = 97 × 36

⇒ X₂ = k / 2²

⇒ X₂ = (97 × 36) ÷ 4

⇒ X₂ = 97 × 9 = 873

**∴ The correct answer is 873.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality

If **y ∝ x**, then **y = kx**. The ratio **y/x** remains constant for all pairs of variables.

Inverse Proportionality

If **y ∝ 1/x**, then **xy = k**. The product of the two variables remains constant.

Joint Variation

When a variable depends on two or more other variables, such as **z ∝ xy**, leading to **z = kxy**.</p

questions.question: The 'Tirabhukti' mentioned in Gupta inscriptions corresponds to present-day ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Tirabhukti'** is an ancient term mentioned in Gupta inscriptions referring to a region in present-day Bihar.
 
• The term is derived from Sanskrit, where **'Tira' means bank and 'Bhukti' means enjoyment or territory**, signifying a region associated with riverbanks.
 
• This region was strategically important during the Gupta Empire due to its fertile plains and proximity to the Ganges River.
 
• Historical records suggest that 'Tirabhukti' was part of the administrative structure of the Gupta dynasty, which divided its empire into several provinces or 'Bhuktis.'
 
• Prominent cities in the region during the Gupta period include Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) and Vaishali.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire (circa 320-550 CE) is considered a golden age of Indian culture, art, science, and literature.
 
• It was marked by significant advancements in mathematics, astronomy, and medicine.
 
• The administrative divisions of the empire included provinces called 'Bhuktis,' which were further subdivided into districts called 'Vishayas.'
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra:**
 
 
• Located in modern-day Patna, Pataliputra was a major political and cultural center during the Gupta period.
 
• It served as the capital of several ancient Indian dynasties, including the Mauryas and the Guptas.
 
 
 
• **Vaishali:**
 
 
• An ancient city in Bihar, Vaishali was significant during the Gupta period and earlier.

questions.question: The value of 3 + tan² θ + cot² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ is:

sec² θ cosec² θ = sec² θ + cosec² θ

⇒ 1 + (1 + tan² θ) + (1 + cot² θ) − sec² θ cosec² θ

⇒ 1 + sec² θ + cosec² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ

Since sec² θ cosec² θ = sec² θ + cosec² θ:

questions.question: Vijay’s salary was first reduced by 16% and subsequently raised by 11%. What percentage was his final salary lower compared to his initial salary?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Percentage** formula: a + b + (a × b)/100

Here, a = −16% (reduction) and b = +11% (increase).

Net change = −16 + 11 + (−16 × 11)/100 = −5 − 1.76 = −6.76%.

The negative sign indicates that the final salary is **lower**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.76%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial reduction = 16%, Subsequent increase = 11%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f0937296f4e760e1463e9dcdb624bf16a9e0abe0311f38c46515bd65fdd8277.png] 

⇒ Let the **initial salary** be 100.

⇒ Salary after 16% reduction = 100 − 16 = 84.

⇒ Salary after 11% increase = 84 + (11% of 84) = 84 + 9.24 = 93.24.

⇒ Total decrease = 100 − 93.24 = 6.76.

⇒ Percentage lower = (6.76 / 100) × 100 = 6.76%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.76%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net effective change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Base Value Change

In percentage problems, 100 is often the best assumed base value to simplify calculations as percentage values directly represent absolute values.

Net Decrease vs Net Increase

If the final result of the successive formula is positive, it indicates a net increase; if negative, it indicates a net decrease or lower value.</p

__

• This marks a significant **decline from the TFR of** **2.2** reported during **NFHS-4 (2015-16)**.
 
• The TFR decline is an indicator of increasing awareness about family planning and better access to contraceptive methods.
 
• The survey also highlights that **urban areas have a lower TFR (1.6)** compared to rural areas (2.1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR):**

 
 
• TFR is defined as the average number of children a woman would have during her lifetime.
 
• It is a key demographic indicator used to assess population growth and replacement levels.
 
• The replacement level of fertility is generally considered to be **2.1 children per woman**, which ensures stable population levels.
 
 
 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS):**
 
 
• NFHS is a nationwide survey conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, in collaboration with the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS).
 
• It provides essential data on health, nutrition, family planning, and demographic indicators.
 
• NFHS surveys play a crucial role in policy formulation and program implementation.
 
 
 
• **Factors influencing TFR:**
 
 
• Improved access to family planning methods and contraceptives.
 
• Better education levels, especially among women.

questions.question: Deepesh has 168 litres of Oil A and 234 litres of Oil B. He fills a number of identical containers with the two types of oil in a manner that each container has only one type of oil, and all containers are completely filled. What can be the maximum volume (in litres) of each container that Deepesh uses, so that all the oil that Deepesh has, of both the types, can be poured into these containers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum volume** of each identical container, calculate the **HCF (Highest Common Factor)** of the given quantities.

Quantity of **Oil A** = 168 litres

Quantity of **Oil B** = 234 litres

Difference = 234 − 168 = 66 litres

HCF must be a factor of 66. Factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 22, 33, 66. Checking 6: 168/6 = 28 and 234/6 = 39. Both are divisible.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Volume of **Oil A** = 168 litres; Volume of **Oil B** = 234 litres.

**Formula:** Maximum capacity of container = **HCF** of (Volume A, Volume B).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d04b0d3baadcc10537496f3db1d641ae7d091bbec7b4f55e8d0cb69b89ff40a.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 168 = 2³ × 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 234 = 2 × 3² × 13

⇒ HCF (168, 234) = 2¹ × 3¹

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is also known as **GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)**.

Number of Containers

If the question asks for the minimum number of containers, divide the total volume by the HCF. **Total containers** = (168/6) + (234/6) = 28 + 39 = 67.

LCM vs HCF

Use **HCF** when dividing or partitioning into equal parts. Use **LCM** when finding a common multiple or meeting point in time/distance.</p

questions.question: {If} x - (1)/(x) = 3, {then the value of} x⁴ + (1)/(x⁴) {is:}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2.

Given k = 3 ⇒ x² + 1/x² = 3² + 2 = 11.

For higher power, x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2.

∴ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 11² − 2 = 121 − 2 = 119.

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x − 1/x = 3

**Formula Used:** (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab and (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ **Squaring both sides** of x − 1/x = 3:

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 3²

⇒ x² + 1/x² − 2 × x × (1/x) = 9

⇒ x² + 1/x² − 2 = 9

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 11

⇒ Now, **squaring both sides** of x² + 1/x² = 11:

⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 11²

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 × x² × (1/x²) = 121

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 = 121

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 121 − 2 = 119

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Reciprocal Identities

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. This is used when the starting sign is positive.

Power Relation

To find x⁴ + 1/x⁴, we always square the expression for x² + 1/x² and subtract 2, regardless of the original sign of (x ± 1/x).

General Form for xⁿ

The process of **successive squaring** allows finding values for x², x⁴, x⁸, and so on, by iterating the k² − 2 or k² + 2 logic.</p

questions.question: The ratio of incomes of Seema and Darshan is 7 : 8. They save ₹15,000 and ₹9,000, respectively. If the ratio of their expenditures is 11 : 16, then what is the total expenditure (in ₹) of Seema and Darshan?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Cross-Multiplication Method** on **Income**, **Expenditure**, and **Savings**.

Income ratio (7 : 8) and Expenditure ratio (11 : 16) with Savings (15,000 : 9,000).

Cross product 1: (7 × 16) − (8 × 11) = 112 − 88 = 24 units.

Cross product 2: (11 × 9,000) − (16 × 15,000) = 99,000 − 240,000 = 141,000 (absolute value).

24 units = ₹141,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹5,875. Seema income = 7 × 5,875 = ₹41,125; Darshan income = 8 × 5,875 = ₹47,000.

Total Expenditure = (41,125 − 15,000) + (47,000 − 9,000) = 26,125 + 38,000 = ₹64,125.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹64,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **Income** = 7 : 8, Ratio of **Expenditure** = 11 : 16, **Savings** = ₹15,000 and ₹9,000.

⇒ Let the **Incomes** of **Seema** and **Darshan** be 7x and 8x.

⇒ (7x − 15,000) ÷ (8x − 9,000) = 11 ÷ 16

⇒ 16 × (7x − 15,000) = 11 × (8x − 9,000)

⇒ 112x − 240,000 = 88x − 99,000

⇒ 24x = 141,000

⇒ x = 141,000 ÷ 24 = 5,875

⇒ Darshan's Expenditure = 8(5,875) − 9,000 = 47,000 − 9,000 = ₹38,000

⇒ Total Expenditure = 26,125 + 38,000 = ₹64,125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹64,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Rakesh invests a sum of ₹5,000 and Shivam invests a sum of ₹9,000 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Shivam gets ₹360 more interest than Rakesh, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Principal** = ₹9,000 − ₹5,000 = ₹4,000

Interest difference for **3 years** = ₹360

Interest difference for **1 year** = 360 ÷ 3 = ₹120

**Rate of Interest** = (Interest difference for 1 year ÷ Principal difference) × 100

Rate % = (120 ÷ 4,000) × 100 = 3%

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Principal of **Shivam** (PS) = ₹9,000

Time (T) = 3 years

Interest difference = ₹360

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9a8209eff41769cab9863cccb2473d8ede4c08dedf23dbf96d513910ba78690.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for Shivam − Interest for Rakesh = 360

⇒ [(9000 × R × 3) ÷ 100] − [(5000 × R × 3) ÷ 100] = 360

⇒ 270R − 150R = 360

⇒ 120R = 360

⇒ R = 360 ÷ 120

⇒ R = 3%

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Relationship

When time and rate are constant, the difference in interest is directly proportional to the difference in principal: ΔSI = (ΔP × R × T) ÷ 100.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for a period is R × T. In this case, the total effective percentage difference is (3 × R)%, which applied to the principal difference gives the total interest difference.

Comparison of SI and CI

Simple Interest remains constant every year on the original principal, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the accumulated amount (Principal + previous Interest).

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 40 kg and that of B and C is 42 kg, then the weight of B (in kg) is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Weight of B** = [2 × (Avg of **A & B**) + 2 × (Avg of **B & C**)] − [3 × (Avg of **A, B & C**)]

⇒ **Weight of B** = [2 × 40 + 2 × 42] − [3 × 45]

⇒ **Weight of B** = [80 + 84] − 135

⇒ **Weight of B** = 164 − 135 = 29 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 29 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **A, B, and C** = 45 kg

Average weight of **A and B** = 40 kg

Average weight of **B and C** = 42 kg

**Formula Used:**

**Total Sum** = **Average** × **Number of items**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b2a17afbe7333cc4fc240857e894556093b54345eda1e1fd9dd4c8a426648f4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Weight (A + B + C)** = 45 × 3 = 135 kg --- (1)

⇒ **Total Weight (A + B)** = 40 × 2 = 80 kg --- (2)

⇒ **Total Weight (B + C)** = 42 × 2 = 84 kg --- (3)

⇒ Adding (2) and (3): (A + B) + (B + C) = 80 + 84

⇒ **A + 2B + C** = 164 kg --- (4)

⇒ Subtracting (1) from (4): (A + 2B + C) − (A + B + C) = 164 − 135

⇒ **Weight of B** = 29 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 29 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Group

If the average of n items is x, then the **Total Sum** is n × x. If one item is shared between two overlapping subgroups, the value of that item equals the sum of the subgroups minus the total sum.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from the **mean** is always zero. This property is used to find missing values in a data set when the average is known.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂, the **Combined Average** = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: What are the wavelength and type of the laser used in a standard CD-ROM drive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**780 nm; infrared laser**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Standard CD-ROM drives use **infrared lasers with a wavelength of 780 nm** to read data encoded on the discs.
 
• The laser interacts with the reflective surface of the CD, detecting pits and lands that represent binary data.
 
• The 780 nm wavelength is optimal for CDs due to the size of the pits and the design of the disc structure.
 
• Infrared lasers are not visible to the human eye but are highly effective for reading older optical media formats such as CDs.
 
• Other optical storage devices like DVDs and Blu-ray discs use lasers with shorter wavelengths, enabling higher data storage capacities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laser Wavelengths in Optical Media:**

 
 
• **DVDs:** Use red lasers with a wavelength of approximately 650 nm, allowing higher data density compared to CDs.
 
• **Blu-ray discs:** Use blue lasers with a wavelength of 405 nm, enabling even greater storage capacity due to smaller pits.
 
 
 
• **Working Principle of Optical Drives:**
 
 
• Data is stored on optical discs in the form of microscopic pits and lands.
 
• The laser beam reads these patterns by detecting changes in reflectivity.
 
• The reflected signal is converted into electrical signals, which are interpreted as binary data.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Radiation:**
 
 
• Infrared radiation is electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves.
 
• It is widely used in communication devices, remote controls, and optical media systems.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Optical Media:**
 
 
• CDs were introduced in the 1980s as a digital replacement for analog audio storage.
 
• DVDs and Blu-ray discs followed, offering higher capacities for video and data storage.
 
• With the advent of solid-state drives (SSDs) and cloud storage, optical media usage has significantly declined.

questions.question: Some marbles are to be packed in four boxes, A, B, C and D, in the proportion of 6 : 3 : 7 : 5. If box B has 400 less marbles than box D, then how many marbles are there in total in all the boxes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of marbles in **Box A : Box B : Box C : Box D** = 6 : 3 : 7 : 5.

Difference between **Box D** and **Box B** in units = 5 − 3 = 2 units.

Given, 2 units = 400 marbles ⇒ 1 unit = 200 marbles.

Total units = 6 + 3 + 7 + 5 = 21 units.

Total marbles = 21 × 200 = 4200.

**∴ The correct answer is 4200 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40cc84060e9c519601ae96b4ad06a3042106de0ee41897a590a1dfa6b9c340ce.png] 

**Given:** Ratio = 6 : 3 : 7 : 5; Difference (D − B) = 400.

**Formula:** Total = Sum of ratio parts × (Value of one part).

⇒ Let the number of marbles in boxes A, B, C, and D be 6x, 3x, 7x, and 5x respectively.

⇒ According to the question: 5x − 3x = 400

⇒ 2x = 400

⇒ x = 200

⇒ Total marbles = 6x + 3x + 7x + 5x = 21x

⇒ Total marbles = 21 × 200 = 4200

**∴ The correct answer is 4200 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

If a quantity is divided in the ratio a : b : c : d, then the parts are ax, bx, cx, and dx where x is the common multiplier.

Difference Rule

The difference between two parts in a ratio is proportional to the difference in their ratio units. (Value Difference ÷ Ratio Difference) gives the value of 1 unit.

Sum of Ratios

The total quantity is always the product of the sum of ratio terms and the value of a single unit.</p

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 79, 92, 39, 57, 91, 28, 74, 90 and 44 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the **assumed mean** be 60.

Calculate **deviations** from 60: +19, +32, −21, −3, +31, −32, +14, +30, −16.

Sum of **deviations** = 19 + 32 − 21 − 3 + 31 − 32 + 14 + 30 − 16 = +54.

Average **deviation** = 54 ÷ 9 = +6.

Actual **Arithmetic Mean** = 60 + 6 = 66.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Observations** = 79, 92, 39, 57, 91, 28, 74, 90, 44

Total **count** (n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

**Arithmetic Mean** = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/311d34e096a2081c41cc97744ba62b23493ec76290fa088db10ba50358d7f167.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 79 + 92 + 39 + 57 + 91 + 28 + 74 + 90 + 44

⇒ Sum = 594

⇒ **Arithmetic Mean** = 594 ÷ 9

⇒ **Arithmetic Mean** = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The sum of the **deviations** of all items from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero, i.e., Σ(xᵢ − Mean) = 0.

Effect of Operations

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every **observation**, the new **mean** will also be increased or decreased by 'k'.

Weighted Arithmetic Mean

When observations have different **importance**, it is calculated as: Mean = Σ(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.</p

__
 
• **Artificially produced elements** are generally radioactive and have unstable nuclei, leading to their short-lived existence.
 
• These elements decay quickly into more stable elements by emitting radiation, which contributes to their short half-lives.
 
• They are primarily synthesized in **laboratories or nuclear reactors** through nuclear reactions such as bombardment of lighter elements with neutrons or high-energy particles.
 
• Many artificially produced elements, such as **Technetium (Tc), Promethium (Pm), and all transuranium elements** (elements beyond Uranium in the periodic table), exhibit this characteristic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Elements:**

 
 
• These are elements not found naturally but produced artificially in laboratories.
 
• Examples include **Plutonium (Pu), Americium (Am), and Curium (Cm)**, among others.
 
 
 
• **Radioactivity:**
 
 
• Radioactive elements emit radiation due to the instability of their atomic nuclei.
 
• This process includes alpha, beta, and gamma radiation emissions.
 
 
 
• **Transuranium Elements:**
 
 
• These are elements with atomic numbers greater than 92 (the atomic number of Uranium).
 
• All transuranium elements are synthetic and exhibit radioactive properties.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Artificial Elements:**
 
 
• Used in medical imaging and cancer treatment (e.g., Technetium-99m).
 
• Act as fuel in nuclear reactors (e.g., Plutonium-239).
 
• Have industrial applications, such as in smoke detectors (e.g., Americium-241).
 
 
 
• **Half-life:**
 
 
• The half-life of a radioactive element is the time it takes for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.
 
• Artificially produced elements often have extremely short half-lives compared to naturally occurring ones.

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 250% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **exterior angles** of any convex polygon is always 360°.

Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + 250% of 360° = 3.5 × 360° = 1260°.

Using the formula (n − 2) × 180° = 1260° ⇒ n − 2 = 7 ⇒ n = 9.

For a **regular polygon**, each interior angle x = 1260° ÷ 9 = 140°.

**∴ The correct answer is 140°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of interior angles is 250% more than the sum of exterior angles.

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°; Sum of exterior angles = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India has set a target to develop a **2 lakh km national highway network** by 2025 under its infrastructure development plan.
 
• The initiative is part of the **Bharatmala Pariyojana**, launched to improve road connectivity across India.
 
• It aims to enhance the efficiency of freight and passenger movement through the development of economic corridors, inter-corridors, feeder routes, and border roads.
 
• This ambitious project focuses on reducing travel time, fuel consumption, and logistics costs, contributing to India's economic growth.
 
• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) is overseeing the implementation of this target.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana:**

 
 
• Bharatmala Pariyojana is a** centrally-sponsored road and highway development initiative launched in 2017**.
 
• The scheme focuses on building a robust highway infrastructure, including economic corridors, rural roads, and expressways.
 
• A budget of approximately ₹5.35 lakh crore was allocated for the first phase of Bharatmala Pariyojana.
 
• The program is expected to cover around 34,800 km of roads in Phase I.
 
 
 
• **Economic Corridors:**
 
 
• Economic corridors are routes designed to facilitate efficient movement of goods and services across regions.
 
• They link production centers, markets, and ports to boost trade and industrial growth.
 
• The development of such corridors under Bharatmala aims to reduce logistics costs and enhance supply chain efficiency.
 
 
 
• **National Highway Authority of India (NHAI):**
 
 
• NHAI is an autonomous agency under MoRTH responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of India's national highways.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in implementing large-scale highway projects, including Bharatmala Pariyojana.
 
• NHAI uses innovative financing methods, such as toll-operate-transfer (TOT) and hybrid annuity models, to fund infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Future Impacts:**
 
 
• The expansion of the national highway network will significantly reduce travel time and improve connectivity in remote areas.
 
• It is expected to boost tourism, trade, and industrial growth across the country.
 
• The project will create thousands of jobs and contribute to India's GDP growth.
